title: Power-Seeking Without Optimality: Do Random and Heuristic Policies Also Drift Toward Power?

original_idea.body:
# Power-Seeking Without Optimality

Compare power-routing across optimal, near-optimal, epsilon-greedy, random, satisficing policies in small MDPs.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: extends the most-cited power-seeking result to sub-optimal agents we actually build.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Small enumerable MDPs, policy simulation on CPU; ideal beginner research.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped comparison across policy classes with clear fraction-visiting-power metric.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Neglected long-horizon instrumental-convergence question, CPU-only, ideal external work.

novelty.reasoning: The optimality caveat is noted in follow-ups but a systematic sub-optimal-policy sweep may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Optimality caveat discussed; systematic empirical sweep may be open.
